parts:
Hello all,

I'm hoping there is a meta-analytic SEM expert on this list to answer
this question. I'm working on a 2-stage meta-analytic SEM study with
dependent correlations in my primary studies.

In stage 1, I'm pooling my correlations using an appropriate
multivariate/multilevel model to account for the dependencies fit by
the "metafor::rma.mv()" model (see below).

In stage 2, I use "metaSEM::wls()" to fit an SEM model onto my pooled
correlation matrix (see below).

**Question: In stage 2, I wonder which of the following options
should be used for "n=" in "wls(..., n=???)" :

(A) sum(a single "n" from each study) # my data below is in long-format
(B) sum("n" from all rows in each study)

Thank you, Simon

#--- Reproducible code and data:
library(metafor)
library(metSEM)

tmp <- rcalc(ri ~ var1 + var2 | study, ni=ni, data=dat.craft2003)
V <- tmp$V
dat <- tmp$dat

dat$var1.var2 <- factor(dat$var1.var2,
levels=c("acog.perf", "asom.perf",
"conf.perf", "acog.asom", "acog.conf", "asom.conf"))

stage1 <- rma.mv(yi~ var1.var2 - 1, V,
random = ~ var1.var2 | study, struct="UN",
data=dat)

pooled_mat <- vec2mat(coef(stage1), dimnames=c("perf", "acog", "asom", "conf"))

sampling_cov <- vcov(stage1)

model = '
conf ~ acog
conf ~ asom
perf ~ conf
perf ~ asom
perf ~ acog
asom ~~ 0*acog

acog ~~ 1*acog
asom ~~ 1*asom'

RAM <- lavaan2RAM(model,
A.notation = "on", S.notation = "with")

stage2 <- wls(Cov=pooled_mat, aCov=sampling_cov,
RAM = RAM, n = ?) #----- what should be *n=?*

Hi Simon, 

When  I rum MASEM through Path analysis I use Harmonic mean. This is my code example. 

# This is fake data

# MODEL TBP
# Sample each pairwise meta-analysis  
H_model1 <- c(  575,
                         1045, 785,
                           351, 383, 431,
                          128, 270, 280, 216)


#compute the harmonic mean
H_mean1 <- 1/mean(1/H_model1)
round(H_mean1)

lower <- '
1.000
0.50  1.000
0.49  0.58  1.000
0.48  0.55  0.47 1.000
0.39  0.31  0.29 0.23 1.000
'

matriz.cov <- getCov(lower, names = c("BEH",  "INT", "ATT", "SN", "PBC"))
matriz.cov

model.TPB <-
  '
BEH ~ INT
INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC
SN~~ATT
SN~~PBC
ATT~~PBC

'

model.fit <- sem(model.TPB, sample.cov = matriz.cov, sample.nobs = round(H_mean1)
                 , std.lv=T)

summary(model.fit, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE
        , standardized = TRUE, modindices = T)


round(fitMeasures(model.fit) [c('chisq', 'df', 'pvalue', 'cfi', 'nfi'
                                , 'gfi', 'rmsea', 'srmr')], 3)


## MASEM bootstrap

raw <- gendata::genmvnorm(matriz.cov, k = 7, n = round(H_mean), seed = 123)
cor(raw)

colnames(raw) <- c("BEH", "PCE", "INT", "EC", "ATT", "SN", "PBC")
round(head(raw), 2)

Boot_model <- sem(model.fit, data = raw, se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000)

summary(Boot_model, standardized = T, fit = T, rsquare = T)

#options(scipen = 999)

                                  , 'gfi', 'rmsea', 'srmr')], 3)

parts:
Hi Simon,

When using metaSEM::wls(), the weight in the analysis is determined by the inverse of the sampling covariance matrix of the pooled correlation matrix. It's important to note that the chi-square statistic, its p-value, and the standard errors of the parameter estimates are not affected by the choice of sample size. However, the sample size affects fit indices that involve sample size in their calculations, such as RMSEA and CFI.

The metaSEM::wls() uses the total sample size as the sample size, which follows the multiple-group SEM tradition. However, it may not necessarily be the best choice.

Best,
Mike
